heroLead: The town of Green River sits along the river and rock formation that lent their name to the source rock underlying much of Utah's oil production.
intro: Green River, straddling the Emery and Grand county line along I-70, sits in a geologically distinctive spot — the Green River Formation, exposed dramatically in the cliffs around town, is the same source rock that produces the waxy crude of the Uinta Basin far to the north and informs geologic understanding of oil shale potential across the region. Locally, mineral interests near the town of Green River tend to be more sparsely developed than the dense coal corridor further west in Emery County.

We buy mineral and royalty interests near Green River directly, and because development activity in this specific area can be limited, we will give you an honest assessment of your interest's current status before any offer.

sections.heading: Geologically famous, but not always actively drilled
paragraphs: The Green River Formation is one of the most studied source rocks in North American petroleum geology, but that scientific significance does not automatically translate into dense local drilling activity around the town itself. We check actual production and permitting tied to your specific legal description rather than assuming activity based on the formation's broader reputation.

sections.heading: A crossroads between coal country and the Paradox Basin
paragraphs: Sitting near the boundary between Emery County's coal fields and Grand County's Paradox Basin trend, an interest near Green River could connect to either geologic setting depending on the exact section. We confirm which applies before discussing value, since the two carry very different production profiles.

sections.heading: A history of exploration beyond oil and gas
paragraphs: The cliffs and mesas around Green River have also drawn uranium and other mineral exploration over the decades, and older family deeds in the area occasionally carry reservations tied to that broader mineral history rather than oil and gas alone. We read the reservation and conveyance language on your specific deed carefully, since assuming a modern oil and gas structure applies to an older, broader mineral deed can lead to an inaccurate picture of what you own.

faqs.question: My deed mentions minerals beyond oil and gas. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can. We review the full reservation language on your deed to confirm exactly what mineral rights you hold before quoting.
